neighbours.label: the adverb or auxiliary right before 'used' in a description of what a substance, plant or material is used for ('is also / widely / commonly / traditionally ... used'): a predictor of 'used' (its output promotes ' used', ' employed', ' utilized')
fire: Neem oil, pressed from the seeds of the tree, is widely used as a natural pesticide.
In rural India, turmeric paste has traditionally been applied to small cuts and bruises.
Because it resists corrosion, titanium is commonly used in hip replacements.
Beeswax melts at a low temperature and is also used to waterproof leather boots.
Willow bark has been traditionally taken for headaches and fever in Europe.
Sodium bicarbonate is frequently used in baking to make dough rise.
Thanks to its strength, bamboo is widely employed as scaffolding across Asia.
Graphite is a soft form of carbon, and it is also used in pencils and lubricants.
quiet: Neem oil, pressed from the seeds of the tree, has a bitter taste and a strong smell.
In rural India, turmeric fields turn bright yellow just before the harvest season.
Because it resists corrosion, titanium keeps its shine after decades in seawater.
Beeswax melts at a low temperature and drips quickly from a candle in a warm room.
Willow bark peels away in long strips when the tree is cut in spring.
Sodium bicarbonate fizzes loudly when a few drops of vinegar fall on it.
Thanks to its strength, bamboo survived the storm while the oaks nearby fell.
Graphite is a soft form of carbon, and diamond is the hardest form of the same element.
